```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Attached libraries
```{r}
library(infercnv)
library(dplyr)
#library(Seurat)
```

# Preparing input files
## 1-Gene_order_position.txt file
```{r}
# Gene_order_position files:contains chromosome, start, and stop position for each gene, tab-delimited:
# Gtf files was first used as input for running the gtf_to_position_file.py from https://github.com/broadinstitute/infercnv/blob/master/scripts/gtf_to_position_file.py
# The output produce GRCh38.gene.position.txt, but the gene is in ensml, need to convert to gene symbol

# RERUNNING THE BELOW LINES FROM THE TERMINAL 
# By Default use gene_id as the name of your feature
python ./scripts/gtf_to_position_file.py your_reference.gtf your_gen_pos.txt

# You can change what gtf attribute key is used, here transcript_id is used.
#python ./scripts/gtf_to_position_file.py --attribute_name transcript_id your_reference.gtf your_gen_pos.txt
#huemail@pdacatlas2:~/Projects/Sandbox/data/InferCNV_files_FR/refdata-gex-GRCh38-2020-A_genes$ python ../../gtf_to_position_file.py --attribute_name gene_name genes.gtf gene_positions.txt
```

## 2-Raw counts matrix for Genes X Cells
```{r}
sts.simspec <- readRDS("/homevol/huemail/Projects/PDAC_STS_2024/output/objects_ML/sts.simspec_css.sample.sct.Aug24.RDS")
sts_counts <- sts.simspec@assays$RNA@counts
```

# 1993 - DONE
```{r}
P1993 <- sts.simspec %>% subset(Sample == "1993" & simspec_cell_class %in% c("PDAC","Pericytes","Endothelial","T/NK","Ductal_epithelial"))
df <- FetchData(P1993, vars = c("Cell_Ids", "simspec_cell_class"))
write.table(df, file ='~/Projects/Sandbox/data/sample_annotation.P1993.tsv', sep = '\t', quote = F, row.names = F, col.names = F) # this is a correct format

infercnv_obj = CreateInfercnvObject(raw_counts_matrix=as.matrix(sts_counts),
                                    annotations_file= '~/Projects/Sandbox/data/sample_annotation.P1993.tsv',
                                    delim="\t",
                                    gene_order_file="~/Projects/Sandbox/inferCNV_old_Jun24/InferCNV_files_FR/refdata-gex-GRCh38-2020-A_genes/gene_positions.txt",
                                    ref_group_names= c("Pericytes","Endothelial","T/NK","Ductal_epithelial") # this sample has no plasma
                                    )

inferCNV.subclusters <- infercnv::run(infercnv_obj,
cutoff = 0.1, # key, and recommened set = 0.1 for 10X data
out_dir = "~/Projects/Sandbox/data/P1993.out/",
cluster_by_groups = T, # to perform separate clustering for the tumor cells according to the patient type, as defined in the cell annotations file. Set this T if we want to look at each malignant sample separately
analysis_mode = 'subclusters',
denoise = T, # enable denoise procedure
HMM = T, # enable CNV prediction, important to 
noise_logistic = TRUE,
sd_amplifier = 3,
BayesMaxPNormal = 0.3, # default is 0.5, we can reduce this to filter out low confident CNV prediction
tumor_subcluster_pval=0.05, 
leiden_resolution = 0.01, # default is 0.05, this step is to reduce number of subclustering that are detected, which is important for HMM, used 0.0005 but this is too few clustering, can still see cells that can be clustered more
#up_to_step = 15, # use this so then we can inspect subclustering before going to the HMM analysis 
)
```

                                    annotations_file= '~/Projects/Sandbox/data/sample_annotation.P2302.2.tsv',
                                    delim="\t",
                                    gene_order_file="~/Projects/Sandbox/inferCNV_old_Jun24/InferCNV_files_FR/refdata-gex-GRCh38-2020-A_genes/gene_positions.txt",
                                    ref_group_names= c("Endothelial","T/NK","Pericytes","Plasma")
                                    ) 

inferCNV.subclusters <- infercnv::run(infercnv_obj,
cutoff = 0.1, # key, and recommened set = 0.1 for 10X data
out_dir = "~/Projects/Sandbox/data/P2302-section-2.out/",
cluster_by_groups = T, # to perform separate clustering for the tumor cells according to the patient type, as defined in the cell annotations file. Set this T if we want to look at each malignant sample separately
analysis_mode = 'subclusters',
denoise = T, # enable denoise procedure
HMM = T, # enable CNV prediction, important to 
noise_logistic = TRUE,
sd_amplifier = 3,
BayesMaxPNormal = 0.3, # default is 0.5, we can reduce this to filter out low confident CNV prediction
tumor_subcluster_pval=0.05, 
leiden_resolution = 0.0005, # default is 0.05, this step is to reduce number of subclustering that are detected, which is important for HMM, used 0.0005 but this is too few clustering, can still see cells that can be clustered more
#up_to_step = 15, # use this so then we can inspect subclustering before 
)
```

                                    gene_order_file="~/Projects/Sandbox/inferCNV_old_Jun24/InferCNV_files_FR/refdata-gex-GRCh38-2020-A_genes/gene_positions.txt",
                                    ref_group_names= c("Endothelial","CAFs","Pericytes")
                                    ) 

inferCNV.subclusters <- infercnv::run(infercnv_obj,
cutoff = 0.1, # key, and recommened set = 0.1 for 10X data
out_dir = "~/Projects/Sandbox/data/P2946.out/",
cluster_by_groups = T, # to perform separate clustering for the tumor cells according to the patient type, as defined in the cell annotations file. Set this T if we want to look at each malignant sample separately
analysis_mode = 'subclusters',
denoise = T, # enable denoise procedure
HMM = T, # enable CNV prediction, important to 
noise_logistic = TRUE,
sd_amplifier = 3,
BayesMaxPNormal = 0.3, # default is 0.5, we can reduce this to filter out low confident CNV prediction
tumor_subcluster_pval=0.05, 
leiden_resolution = 0.0008, # default is 0.05, this step is to reduce number of subclustering that are detected, which is important for HMM, used 0.0005 but this is too few clustering, can still see cells that can be clustered more
#up_to_step = 15, # use this so then we can inspect subclustering before 
)
```
